spec_match.rationale: Reading conditionText from CSSContainerRule and splitting top-level commas is real CSSOM territory, but the page asserts a 'Chrome 149+ rule.conditions[]' attribute whose existence is unverified against css-conditional-5 IDL, and its own comma-separated sample rules are parser-dropped in pre-150 browsers without acknowledgment.

interactive.rationale: The Scan button walks real stylesheets, recurses grouping rules, populates summary chips, renders per-rule cards with conditionText/containerName/cssText, and shows an honest conditions[]-missing compat note.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises CSSOM walking, conditionText splitting and a conditions[] check — exactly what the page does.

edge_cases.rationale: Cross-origin sheets, grouping-rule recursion, no-rules and missing-conditions[] states are all handled, but the biggest edge — the comma rules themselves being dropped by a pre-150 parser so the inspector silently under-counts — is not detected or explained.

references.rationale: The see-also section links only sibling concepts; there is no chromestatus.com/feature/6196591858941952 link anywhere on the page, violating invariant 3 (the self-heal anchor).

conformance.rationale: The shared feature suite tests real parse/round-trip contracts and honestly fails 4 of 5 in this pre-150 browser.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Verified via headless Chromium 141 cloud fallback (full-page screenshot + DOM, not chrome-devtools-mcp): page renders with clean empty state and 1/4/0 conformance panel; the Scan button was not driven, so the rule-card rendering and compat note were reviewed from code only.

telemetry_health.rationale: Baseline injected telemetry only; the scan results and conditions[]-availability signal are not reported as events.

design_system.rationale: All colours are variables, the scan button sets background and color together, and badge variants keep AA-safe pairings.

accessibility.rationale: The single control is a native button, but scan results replace the inspector body with no live region or focus management, and the summary chips update silently.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Chips and rows wrap, long values word-break, and code blocks scroll horizontally; renders clean at 1280px headless but the ≈360px touch viewport was not exercised.

openQuestions.title: Add the missing chromestatus.com/feature/6196591858941952 link
openQuestions.detail: Invariant 3 requires every page to cite its ChromeStatus entry — it is the slug-recovery self-heal anchor. This page's see-also has only sibling links. Add the ChromeStatus (and ideally the css-conditional-5 container-rule) reference.

openQuestions.title: Verify rule.conditions[] against the spec and shipped IDL
openQuestions.detail: The page and feature index both claim CSSContainerRule gains a conditions attribute in Chrome 149+. css-conditional-5's published IDL exposes conditionText/containerName/containerQuery; a conditions array is not obviously part of the shipped change. Confirm in the spec and Chromium source (runtime IDL) — if it does not exist, drop the 'Chrome 149+' claim and keep the manual splitter as the canonical approach; if it does, cite the spec section.

openQuestions.title: Detect parser-dropped comma rules and say so
openQuestions.detail: This page defines four @container sample rules, three comma-separated. In a pre-150 browser those three never reach the CSSOM, so a scan reports '1 rule, 0 multi' with no hint why — the inspector silently demonstrates nothing. The page knows it authored 4 rules: compare found-vs-authored counts (or CSS.supports a comma list, as the conformance suite does) and surface a 'comma rules were dropped by this parser — requires Chrome 150+' notice.

openQuestions.title: Announce scan results to assistive tech
openQuestions.detail: Wrap the summary chips and inspector body in aria-live=polite (or move focus to the results heading after scan) so the scan outcome is perceivable without vision.

summary: Reviewed with the headless-Chromium-141 cloud fallback (not chrome-devtools-mcp): full-page screenshot + DOM of /v149/comma-separated-container-queries/conditions-api/ and the feature /conformance/ route (HTTP 200; panel 1 pass / 4 fail / 0 blocked, honestly reflecting pre-150 support). The inspector tool itself is well built — real CSSOM walk, paren-depth comma splitter, honest conditions[]-missing note, escaped output — but the page breaks invariant 3 (no ChromeStatus link), claims an unverified conditions[] API as 'Chrome 149+', and silently under-reports when the browser's parser drops its own comma-separated sample rules. The Scan interaction was not driven headless.
